{
  "findings": [
    {
      "file": "sentry-repo",
      "line": 1,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Accidental git submodule added",
      "body": "The PR adds a gitlink/submodule entry `sentry-repo` pointing at commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a. This is unrelated to the upsampling feature and introduces an unwanted submodule, which can break clones or repository tooling. Remove it before merging."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py",
      "line": 1048,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "upsampled_count can undercount or return NULL when sample_weight is missing",
      "body": "The new aggregate computes `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with no null/default handling. If any row in an allowlisted project query has missing or NULL `sample_weight` (older SDK events, events without error-sampling context, or non-error rows included by mistake), those rows contribute zero or the aggregate may become NULL, causing silently wrong error counts. Use a default such as coalesce/ifNull(sample_weight, 1) or prove the column is always populated."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/search/events/datasets/discover.py",
      "line": 1042,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "api",
      "title": "upsampled_count is exposed as a public query function",
      "body": "The `upsampled_count` SnQL function is added without `private=True`. If it is selectable through public query APIs, callers can bypass the allowlist and dataset guards and request upsampled counts in contexts where they are not valid, causing incorrect results or query failures. Mark it private if it is only meant for internal rewriting."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py",
      "line": 137,
      "severity": "high",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Discover error-focus detection uses unsafe substring match",
      "body": "`_is_error_focused_query` returns true whenever the raw query contains `event.type:error`. This also matches negated filters like `!event.type:error`, mixed queries like `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and text inside quoted values. For discover queries this can rewrite count() for non-error data and produce wrong counts. Parse the query or require a strictly error-only condition."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py",
      "line": 221,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Upsampling decision ignores the actual scoped dataset and query",
      "body": "`_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` and `query`, but the eligibility check uses the outer `dataset` and original HTTP request. In split/fallback paths the executed query can have additional conditions or a different dataset, so the upsampling decision can be made from stale context. Pass the actual scoped dataset and final query to the eligibility helper."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/helpers/error_upsampling.py",
      "line": 27,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "data",
      "title": "Eligibility cache key is lossy and not invalidated when the allowlist changes",
      "body": "The cache key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`, which is a lossy key: different project sets can collide and Python's built-in hash is not meant to be a stable external identifier. The cache also has no automatic invalidation when the allowlist option changes; `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is unused. This can reuse an eligibility result for the wrong projects or serve stale allowlist state. Use an explicit key such as sorted IDs joined or SHA-256, and wire invalidation or remove the dead helper."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_events_stats.py",
      "line": 259,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Top-event ordering is not transformed for upsampling",
      "body": "When upsampling is enabled for top events, only the y-axis columns are rewritten. The `orderby` value passed to top-events queries is not transformed, so if the request orders by count() the top-N selection can be based on raw counts while the returned series use upsampled counts. Transform or validate ordering expressions as well."
    },
    {
      "file": "tests/snuba/api/endpoints/test_organization_events_stats.py",
      "line": 3554,
      "severity": "medium",
      "category": "test_gap",
      "title": "Tests do not cover failure modes introduced by upsampling",
      "body": "The endpoint tests only cover explicit `event.type:error` discover queries with allowlisted projects. They do not cover missing/null `sample_weight`, mixed or negated discover filters, the errors dataset, top-event ordering, or cache staleness/invalidation. These are the primary paths where the new transformation can silently change counts, so they need coverage."
    },
    {
      "file": "src/sentry/testutils/factories.py",
      "line": 353,
      "severity": "low",
      "category": "bug",
      "title": "Test factory skips zero sample rates and swallows errors",
      "body": "`_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` uses truthiness, so a valid client_sample_rate of 0 is ignored, and broad exception handling hides malformed contexts. If zero-rate events are meaningful for upsampling, tests will not exercise them. Use an is-not-None check and narrower error handling."
    }
  ]
}

findings.title: Accidental git submodule added
findings.body: The PR adds a gitlink/submodule entry `sentry-repo` pointing at commit a5d290951def84afdcc4c88d2f1f20023fc36e2a. This is unrelated to the upsampling feature and introduces an unwanted submodule, which can break clones or repository tooling. Remove it before merging.

findings.title: upsampled_count can undercount or return NULL when sample_weight is missing
findings.body: The new aggregate computes `toInt64(sum(sample_weight))` with no null/default handling. If any row in an allowlisted project query has missing or NULL `sample_weight` (older SDK events, events without error-sampling context, or non-error rows included by mistake), those rows contribute zero or the aggregate may become NULL, causing silently wrong error counts. Use a default such as coalesce/ifNull(sample_weight, 1) or prove the column is always populated.

findings.title: upsampled_count is exposed as a public query function
findings.body: The `upsampled_count` SnQL function is added without `private=True`. If it is selectable through public query APIs, callers can bypass the allowlist and dataset guards and request upsampled counts in contexts where they are not valid, causing incorrect results or query failures. Mark it private if it is only meant for internal rewriting.

findings.title: Discover error-focus detection uses unsafe substring match
findings.body: `_is_error_focused_query` returns true whenever the raw query contains `event.type:error`. This also matches negated filters like `!event.type:error`, mixed queries like `event.type:error OR event.type:transaction`, and text inside quoted values. For discover queries this can rewrite count() for non-error data and produce wrong counts. Parse the query or require a strictly error-only condition.

findings.title: Upsampling decision ignores the actual scoped dataset and query
findings.body: `_get_event_stats` receives `scoped_dataset` and `query`, but the eligibility check uses the outer `dataset` and original HTTP request. In split/fallback paths the executed query can have additional conditions or a different dataset, so the upsampling decision can be made from stale context. Pass the actual scoped dataset and final query to the eligibility helper.

findings.title: Eligibility cache key is lossy and not invalidated when the allowlist changes
findings.body: The cache key uses `hash(tuple(sorted(snuba_params.project_ids)))`, which is a lossy key: different project sets can collide and Python's built-in hash is not meant to be a stable external identifier. The cache also has no automatic invalidation when the allowlist option changes; `invalidate_upsampling_cache` is unused. This can reuse an eligibility result for the wrong projects or serve stale allowlist state. Use an explicit key such as sorted IDs joined or SHA-256, and wire invalidation or remove the dead helper.

findings.title: Top-event ordering is not transformed for upsampling
findings.body: When upsampling is enabled for top events, only the y-axis columns are rewritten. The `orderby` value passed to top-events queries is not transformed, so if the request orders by count() the top-N selection can be based on raw counts while the returned series use upsampled counts. Transform or validate ordering expressions as well.

findings.title: Tests do not cover failure modes introduced by upsampling
findings.body: The endpoint tests only cover explicit `event.type:error` discover queries with allowlisted projects. They do not cover missing/null `sample_weight`, mixed or negated discover filters, the errors dataset, top-event ordering, or cache staleness/invalidation. These are the primary paths where the new transformation can silently change counts, so they need coverage.

findings.title: Test factory skips zero sample rates and swallows errors
findings.body: `_set_sample_rate_from_error_sampling` uses truthiness, so a valid client_sample_rate of 0 is ignored, and broad exception handling hides malformed contexts. If zero-rate events are meaningful for upsampling, tests will not exercise them. Use an is-not-None check and narrower error handling.
